newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa in late surge, builds up momentum.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa in late surge, builds up momentum.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures motored higher in Wednesday on late trade short-covering with the market building up further upward momentum after the last week's sharp retracement.
After surrendering some early gains on the back of soaring sterling against German mark, the market rebuilt some strength in the afternoon to flip much higher.
In mid-morning, sterling eclipsed Tuesday's six-year high to reach a fresh peak at 2.9760 marks. But the sterling shed some ground in the afternoon.
German traders said on Wednesday cocoa processors were buying replacing cover to feed relatively active plants, undeterred by sterling's strength against the mark.
Traders reported some trades of afloat and local stock material which they said showed consumer cover was slow.
Benchmark September climbed to the day's peak of 1,059 stg a tonne before ending at 1,057, a 14 gain on the day. The contract held at just below 1,050 for the most part of the day.
But it stood shy of the immediate resistance at 1,060.
A major barrier lies at the 1,087-1,108 chart gap, a level some bulls say was now within reach.
"It's a constructive close today," said one.
Support is established at 1,000, the lows seen last week after the blistering rally that pushed values to one-year peak of 1,170 stg a few days earlier.

Broker GNI said overnight news from Abidjan which put Ivorian cocoa arrivals at 1.05-1.06 million tonnes up to July 4 against 1.148 million last year could be viewed by some as a sign of lower supply.
"But this ignores the fact that virtually no mid-crop cocoa has yet been delivered," it said in a commentary.
Overall volume, including crosses on March 1998, stood at 6,192 lots.
